business_model: Freemium SaaS, browser-based real-time collaborative design tool

historical_evidence.company: Founded 2012 by Dylan Field and Evan Wallace, a browser-based, real-time collaborative interface-design tool, positioned as a multiplayer alternative to traditional single-user design software.
historical_evidence.market: Design and collaborative-work-tooling market, with the product's real-time multiplayer approach and browser-native architecture positioned as a structurally different technical approach than incumbent, locally-installed design software.
historical_evidence.team: Founders had operated the company since 2012, with several prior funding rounds establishing an escalating quality of investor backing by the snapshot date.
historical_evidence.product: Real-time, multi-user collaborative design tool running in the browser, with reported expanding use cases beyond interface design into visual whiteboarding, diagramming, and presentation creation — organic usage expansion into adjacent workflows is itself a meaningful product-strength signal.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised $50M in Series D funding on April 30, 2020, led by Andreessen Horowitz with participation from Durable Capital and existing backers Index Ventures, Greylock, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, and Founders Fund, at a $2 billion valuation — a roughly 4.5x valuation increase from its $440M Series C valuation in 2019, a very rapid one-year step-up.
historical_evidence.traction: Contemporaneous coverage noted increased Figma engagement coinciding with the early-2020 shift toward remote work as the pandemic began — a real, timely usage-momentum signal, though no specific user-count, revenue, or NRR figures were found in the sources reviewed for the snapshot date.
historical_evidence.financial: The scale and speed of the valuation step-up (4.5x in roughly one year), combined with a syndicate including nearly every major tier-one venture firm across multiple rounds, is a strong signal of sustained, broad-based investor conviction, though no specific revenue or margin figures were found for this snapshot.

sources.title: Figma raises $50 million Series D led by Andreessen Horowitz

future_outcome.outcome_summary: Figma continued rapid growth, was the subject of a proposed $20 billion Adobe acquisition announced in 2022 that was ultimately abandoned in late 2023 due to regulatory opposition, and subsequently completed its own IPO.

benchmark_notes.why_included: The portfolio's clearest, least-controversial Elite-tier positive control — used deliberately sparingly (only one such unambiguous case, alongside Stripe as a Strong/Elite anchor) to avoid the original audit's over-concentration in famous, obviously-great companies. Tests whether SIE's scoring ceiling behaves sensibly for a company where nearly every available signal (valuation trajectory, investor quality and breadth, organic usage-expansion pattern) points the same strong direction, without manufacturing false 90+ scores merely because the evidence happens to be abundant and uniformly positive (see the SPS-distribution-philosophy discussion on how rare 90+ should be, addressed separately in this portfolio's README).
benchmark_notes.known_ambiguities: None of particular note for this record; genuinely one of the more straightforward cases in the portfolio.
benchmark_notes.evidence_limitations: No user-count, revenue, or NRR figures specific to the April 2020 snapshot were located in the sources reviewed; the primary evidentiary basis is the funding/valuation trajectory and qualitative usage-momentum commentary rather than direct usage metrics.
